assertions.interpretation: The main scene is set when Gu Rong was in Luoyang and once accepted someone's invitation to a banquet.
During the banquet, Gu Rong noticed the roast-server showing a desire for the roast, an event occurring within the scene.
His fellow diners mocked him at the same time, contemporaneous with the giving of the roast.
Later, after the chaos (of the fall of the Western Jin), Gu Rong crossed the Yangtze River — a later outcome relative to the banquet scene.

assertions.interpretation: During each crisis after crossing the river, a man repeatedly assisted Gu Rong — a recurring later outcome.

assertion.interpretation: Gu Rong then gave his own portion to the roast-server, a sequential action within the banquet scene.

assertion.interpretation: Gu Rong's quoted remark at the banquet, referring to the roast-server holding the roast all day without knowing its taste.

assertion.interpretation: Upon asking the reason, Gu Rong learned the helper was the very roast-server — the resolution of the later outcome.
